summary.name: TICS
summary.one_liner: TICS is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that plays mechanical keyboard sounds when you type and mouse sounds when you click, scroll, or drag windows.
use_cases: Add satisfying keyboard sounds while typing on a Mac
Hear clicks and scroll notches from a mouse
Get audio feedback when dragging or resizing windows
Customize keyboard sounds per key or shortcut
Use tactile feedback sounds with a Logitech MX Master 4
summary.what_it_does: TICS runs in the menu bar and plays the sound of a chosen mechanical keyboard for every key pressed in any app, with separate press and release sounds and softer repeats when a key is held. It offers 11 keyboard sound profiles, including Cherry MX, Topre, and Holy Panda styles, plus a synthetic option. Mouse sounds cover clicks, every scroll wheel notch, and dragging, including a ratchet sound when moving or resizing windows. In settings you can adjust pitch, volume, and tone for mouse sounds, and reassign sounds to individual keys, key groups, or shortcuts. For Logitech mice, it can also sound Logi Options+ buttons and, on the MX Master 4, trigger haptic vibration effects.
notable: Open source, code on GitHub at yestoall/tics
11 keyboard sound profiles including Cherry MX, Topre, and Holy Panda
Supports Logitech Options+ button sounds and MX Master 4 haptic effects
Listens only; does not save keystrokes or connect to the internet
caveats: Needs Input Monitoring permission; Bluetooth permission for Logitech features
Logitech Options+ button sounds work over Bluetooth but not with the Bolt receiver
MX Master 4 vibration effects apply only to that mouse model
